result.rationale: The new refreshOAuthTokens.ts adds a fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only method and body — no AbortController/timeout signal. When credential sync is enabled, every OAuth token refresh (Google, HubSpot, O365, Zoom, Webex, Zoho, Lark) routes through this call, so a hung sync endpoint would block those flows indefinitely. This is a real, specific robustness/availability concern grounded in the new code, though not a clear-cut correctness defect since it requires an external misbehaving endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` without an `AbortController` signal or any other timeout mechanism. As written, this request can wait indefinitely at the Node/undici level if the endpoint hangs, and the awaited refresh path (and therefore any calendar operation awaiting refreshed tokens) will remain pending until an external/platform timeout occurs. This is a concrete robustness/reliability concern introduced by the diff, but it’s not a strictly verifiable functional defect in normal conditions (it depends on the endpoint hanging and platform timeouts).
